candidates.why: remove_NOD_item frees _obj->texts[i] at line 1360 then memmove shifts texts[i+1..] into slot i (line 1363). Back in fixup_NOD the for-loop at line 1397 does NOT decrement i, so the next macro in the else-chain re-reads _obj->texts[i] at line 1393 (and line 1388 for the TU path) — now a shifted/stale slot after the free+memmove. Same iteration index used after array mutation.

The loop in fixup_NOD (line 1397) keeps the same i and continues the else-chain, so subsequent DISABLE_NODSTYLE expansions re-index _obj->itemhandles[i] via remove_NOD_item (line 1357 ARGS_REF(_obj->itemhandles[i]) and line 1361) against the shifted array — stale index after free.

In the is_tu branch, bit_convert_TU((BITCODE_TU)_obj->texts[i]) at line 1388 reads _obj->texts[i] which may already have been freed/shifted by a prior remove_NOD_item in the same else-chain (free at 1360, memmove at 1363) since i is not adjusted in the loop at line 1397.
